# SRA ABI Golden Vectors

Canonical `abi.encode(adapter, handler, sourceChainId, Message)` outputs,
generated by Solidity itself. The Rust integration test
`crates/sra-common/tests/golden_vectors.rs` loads each vector and asserts
`sra_common::abi::abi_encode_sra_message(...)` produces byte-identical output.

## Why committed

Committing the JSON keeps the test self-contained — no sibling checkouts, no
CI hooks, no extra tooling to run `cargo test`. The fixtures are **derived**
from the Solidity side, but the Rust side treats them as a frozen contract:
the test doesn't regenerate them, it just compares against them.

## Schema

Each `<name>.json` contains the inputs used on both sides plus the encoded
output. Fields consumed by `golden_vectors.rs` today:

- `adapter`, `handler` — EVM addresses (hex, 0x-prefixed).
- `sourceChainId`, `depositAmount`, `targetChainId`, `targetAmount` —
  decimal strings (survive uint256 values intact through JSON).
- `account`, `appId` — 32-byte hex.
- `initCode`, `extra`, `encoded` — arbitrary hex byte arrays.
- `depositToken`, `targetToken` — EVM addresses.
- `actionIdxs` — array of decimal strings.

Additional fields (`encodedForReplay`, `replayHash`, `description`) are
present for diagnostic purposes and may be consumed by future tests.

`_index.json` lists the vector names; the test iterates this list to find
every file.

## Regenerating

The source of truth is `script/GoldenVectorGenerator.s.sol` in
[sra-stx](https://github.com/zerodevapp/sra-stx). Its `OUT_DIR` and the
foundry `fs_permissions` entry write directly into this directory, so
regeneration is one command:

```bash
cd /path/to/sra-stx
forge script script/GoldenVectorGenerator.s.sol
```

This assumes `sra-stx` and `sra-solana` are checked out as sibling
directories (the generator writes to `../sra-solana/...`). Then run
`cargo test -p sra-common` here; any byte divergence will fail.
